quote: Was it their will, and did they order, that war should be undertaken against king Antiochus, and all who should join his party?
notes: Comitial war-declaration vote against Antiochus gated on religious preliminaries (sacrifices and favourable auspices ordered by the senate); no v1 type covers a war vote, so coded as formal institutional act; quote at livy:en:36:1.

quote: when they were impressed for manning the ships, they appealed to the tribunes of the people, by whom the cause was referred to the senate
notes: Eight maritime colonies (Ostia, Fregenae, etc.) resisted naval impressment and appealed to the tribunes; the senate unanimously denied their claimed exemption; quote at livy:en:36:3.

quote: no senator, nor any who had the privilege of giving an opinion in the senate, nor any of the inferior magistrates, should go so far from the city
notes: Wartime consular edict restricting senators' absence from Rome (no more than five absent at once) to keep the political class mobilized for the Antiochene war; quote at livy:en:36:3.

quote: The Eleans requested aid against the Achaeans; for they supposed, that, since the war had been declared against Antiochus contrary to their judgment
notes: Elis, fearing Achaean attack, appealed to Antiochus, who sent 1,000 foot under Euphanes the Cretan, while the Epirots sent a deliberately hedging embassy; quote at livy:en:36:5.

quote: a decree, disguised under a slight covering of words, was passed in his favour against the Romans
notes: The Boeotian national council, whose polity Livy says was in long socioeconomic decline with many hoping for a change of affairs, voted a veiled decree admitting Antiochus against Rome; quote at livy:en:36:6.

quote: Mnasilochus, a man of distinction among the Acarnanians, being bribed by many presents, not only laboured himself to dispose that nation in favour of the king
notes: Bribed Acarnanian notables Mnasilochus and the praetor Clytus plotted to betray Medio and Thurium to Antiochus; Medio fell by treachery (36:12) but Thurium held and Octavius' arrival steadied the loyalists; quote at livy:en:36:11.

quote: He, therefore, with his wife and children, quitted the kingdom, and retired to Ambracia. Thus all Athamania came under the authority and dominion of Philip.
notes: King Amynander fled to Ambracia as Philip's calculated clemency toward Athamanian prisoners swung his subjects' loyalty, and Athamania passed under Macedonian control; quote at livy:en:36:14.

quote: to request the king again to assemble his land and marine forces and cross over into Greece
notes: The Aetolian council at Hypata sent Thoas and other ambassadors to beg Antiochus to return with his forces or at least supply men and money, which he immediately provided; quote at livy:en:36:26.

quote: their minds were so highly exasperated, both by the harshness of the order and the indignity offered
notes: Though the Apocleti counselled submission after the consul's chains episode (36:28), the Aetolian general assembly, inflamed by Rome's harsh terms and Nicander's assurances of aid from Antiochus, repudiated peace; quote at livy:en:36:29.

quote: the Messenians were willing, both to open their gates, and surrender their city, to the Romans, but not to the Achaeans
notes: Besieged by the Achaeans for refusing to join their confederacy, Messene appealed over their heads to Quinctius, who ordered the siege raised, the exiles recalled, and Messene joined to the league on his arbitration; quote at livy:en:36:31.

quote: Phaeneas himself, with some others of the principal men, instantly came and threw themselves at his feet
notes: The besieged Aetolians at Naupactum appealed as suppliants to Quinctius, who interceded with the consul to grant a truce and allow an Aetolian embassy to surrender to the senate at Rome; quote at livy:en:36:35.

quote: a fast ought to be instituted in honour of Ceres, and the same observed every fifth year
notes: Prodigies (oxen climbing a roof, stone showers, lightning strikes) led the senate to order consultation of the Sibylline books, instituting a new quinquennial fast of Ceres plus supplications and expiatory sacrifices; quote at livy:en:36:37.

quote: The unanimous senate not only gave their vote for the triumph, but by their influence prevailed on the tribune to desist from his protest.
notes: Tribune Sempronius Blaesus moved to postpone Scipio Nasica's Boian triumph until Liguria was subdued (36:39), but after Scipio's rebuttal the senate voted the triumph and induced the tribune to drop his protest; quote at livy:en:36:40.

quote: the elections were held at Rome, in which were chosen consuls, Lucius Cornelius Scipio and Caius Laelius, from whom all men expected the conclusion of the war
notes: Year-end consular and praetorian elections framed by the expectation that the new consuls would finish the Antiochene war; no overt contest narrated here, coded for the electoral stakes of the eastern command; quote at livy:en:36:45.
